exposure: Causes of PPH (uterine atony, placental abnormalities, placenta accreta)
outcome: Incidence and trends of massive transfusions (MTs)
cohort: The study included 3552 postpartum hemorrhage patients who were at least 28 weeks gestation and delivered at Peking University First Hospital between January 2006 and February 2015, with a specific focus on the 106 women who received massive transfusions.
finding: The study found a stable incidence of massive transfusions (MTs) in postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) cases over a decade, but a rising trend in placental abnormalities (especially placenta accreta) as an underlying cause, with placenta accreta carrying the highest risk of hysterectomy.
